questions.question:
Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blanks.

I expect to return _______ Mumbai _______ March 15.
questions.solution:
First, understand the sentence and then choose the correct prepositions.

Option 2 is incorrect because **at** is incorrect here. we use **at** with specific times of the day and specific places in a city.

Option 3 is incorrect because** in** is incorrect for the second blank. We use **in **with only the months of the year [ not attached with the date]

Option 4 is incorrect because both the prepositions are appropriate for the respective blanks.

We use **on **with specific days of the week or year [ March 15]

We use **to** with verbs to show movement such as **go** and **come**.

**From** is used used to show the place/time where someone or something starts

Corrected sentence: *I expect to return** from** Mumbai **on** March 15.*

Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

After three months of practice, I ________ now swim quite fast.
questions.solution:
Let's first understand the words and their usage.

**Cannot** is the opposite of can. 

**Should** and **could** are the past tense of shall and can.

In the given sentence, **now **is mentioned which denotes that the action is in the present tense, so option 2 and 4 are incorrect. The sentence is telling about 3 months of practice and then the ability to perform it **quite fast**. The correct sentence will be:

*After three months of practice, I **can** now swim quite fast.*

Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Either Avika or Nikunj are going to win the prize in the handwriting competition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**are going to'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Here, one must have a basic knowledge of correlative conjunction to check this type of question.
 
• Whenever **either... or** is used, the verb has to agree with the noun, nearest to it.
 
 
• ex: *Either he or she cooks dinner.*
 
• *ex: He either washes the clothes himself or asks her to wash them.*
 
 

The corrected sentence will be like: *Either Avika or Nikunj **is **going to win the prize in the handwriting competition.*

questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word.**

IMPECCABLE
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Imperfect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The antonym of "**impeccable**" is "**imperfect**."
 
• The term "**impeccable**" means** without faults, flaws or errors, perfect or flawless in every aspect.**
 
• **Option 1) "Faultless"** is a synonym of "impeccable" and means without faults or flaws. Therefore, it is not an antonym.
 
• **Option 2) "Unsullied"** means not tarnished or stained, pure or spotless. It is not an antonym of "impeccable."
 
• **Option 3) "Imperfect"** means not perfect, having flaws or defects. It is the opposite of "impeccable." 
 
• **Option 4) "Methodical" **means done according to a systematic or orderly approach. It is not an antonym of "impeccable."
 
• In conclusion, the antonym of "**impeccable**" is "**imperfect**," which means not perfect or having flaws.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Example sentences **using all the words:

 
 
• Her **impeccable **work ethic made her stand out from the rest of the team.** (Impeccable)**
 
• The dress was **faultless**, and not a single thread was out of place. **(Faultless)**
 
• The **unsullied **snow made for a picturesque view. **(Unsullied)**
 
• The painting was beautiful, but the **imperfect **brush strokes detracted from its overall appeal.** (Imperfect)**
 
• He approached the task in a **methodical **way, carefully planning each step.** (Methodical)**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, Select No improvement.**

options.text: for centuries now but in the past
since centuries now but in the past
for centuries now moreover in the past

questions.solution:
The difference between **since** and **for** should be known to answer this question.

**FOR** is used for general periods of time. It’s to express duration.

*I have lived here for ten years*

**SINCE** is used for a starting point, a specific time.

*I have known him since January.*

In the given sentence, centuries is mentioned which is a period of time. So **for **will be used here.

Option 4 is wrong because **moreover** [as a further matter; besides.] is incorrect.

Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

She is always finding fault with the food I cook.
questions.solution:
In the given sentence, one should understand the usage of the verb according to the subject.

Here, "she" is singular so we should use a singular verb.

Also, remember:

"**Always**" is an adverb. It does not affect the form of the verb. The form of the verb depends on the subject, which is a noun, pronoun, nominal phrase, or nominal clause.

For eg:

***He **always **reads** quietly.

**They** always **read** quietly.

The **boy **always **reads **quietly.

The **boys** always **read** quietly.*

Similarly, the correct sentence for the given question will be:

***She** always **finds** fault with the food I cook.*

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The village, with all its houses, were flooded by the river.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **were flooded**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If **two subjects** are separated by **'with**', the** verb** agrees with the **main subject**.

 
 
• For example: The **thief, **with his apprentices, **has** been caught by the police.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, the 'village' is the **main subject**.
 
• As it is a **singular subject**, the **verb** that must agree with it must also be **singular**.
 
• Hence, 'were' must be replaced by 'was' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *The village, with all its houses, **was **flooded by the river.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The list of words that agree with the main subject:
 
 
• As well as
 
• Like
 
• Unlike
 
• Besides
 
• In addition to
 
• **With**
 
• Together with
 
• Along with
 
• Including
 
• Accompanied by
 
• But
